policy_title: Chronic Care Management and Principal Care

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for principal care management (PCM), chronic care management (CCM) and complex CCM services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans may reimburse a PCM charge, CCM charge, or complex CCM charge when all of the applicable Medicare Program requirements are met. Humana requires a provider to follow all PCM and CCM requirements as outlined in the Federal Register and relevant CMS guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined below.

extracted_content.title: Member Pre-Condition
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Member Pre-Condition
extracted_content.content: For PCM services, the member must be diagnosed with one chronic condition that places the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline or that is expected to last at least 3 months or until the death of the patient. For CCM services, the member must be diagnosed with at least two chronic conditions that place the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline and that are expected to last at least 12 months or until the death of the patient.

extracted_content.title: Staff Requirement
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Staff Requirement
extracted_content.content: PCM and CCM services must be performed by clinical staff meeting the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1).

extracted_content.title: Billing Limitations
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Billing Limitations
extracted_content.content: A provider may not simultaneously bill for PCM services and certain other services, including CCM, for the same member. A provider may not bill for PCM services during the surgical global period of a service for which they are reimbursed for the same member. Only one provider may bill for CCM services for a specific member per month. CCM services for a specific member must be billed for either CCM or complex CCM, but not both, per month. A provider may not bill for CCM services rendered to a member during an inpatient facility stay that is coverable by the member's MA plan.

extracted_content.title: Additional Resources on this Topic
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Additional Resources on this Topic
extracted_content.content: Humana's Making it Easier web-based training series includes a video on the proper reporting and reimbursement of CCM and PCM services that may supplement your understanding of this policy.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans may reimburse a PCM charge, CCM charge, or complex CCM charge when all of the applicable Medicare Program requirements are met. Humana requires a provider to follow all PCM and CCM requirements as outlined in the Federal Register and relevant CMS guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined below.

For PCM services, the member must be diagnosed with one chronic condition that places the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline or that is expected to last at least 3 months or until the death of the patient. For CCM services, the member must be diagnosed with at least two chronic conditions that place the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline and that are expected to last at least 12 months or until the death of the patient.

PCM and CCM services must be performed by clinical staff meeting the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1).

A provider may not simultaneously bill for PCM services and certain other services, including CCM, for the same member. A provider may not bill for PCM services during the surgical global period of a service for which they are reimbursed for the same member. Only one provider may bill for CCM services for a specific member per month. CCM services for a specific member must be billed for either CCM or complex CCM, but not both, per month. A provider may not bill for CCM services rendered to a member during an inpatient facility stay that is coverable by the member's MA plan.

Humana's Making it Easier web-based training series includes a video on the proper reporting and reimbursement of CCM and PCM services that may supplement your understanding of this policy.
